practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Rajya Sabha to pass a resolution for creating one or more All-India Services common to the Union and the States?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 312 of the Constitution grants the Rajya Sabha the exclusive power to create new All-India Services if it passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which constitutional article can the Rajya Sabha empower Parliament to legislate on a matter enumerated in the State List in the national interest?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 249 provides that if the Rajya Sabha declares by a resolution supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest that Parliament should make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List, Parliament is competent to make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the majority required in the Rajya Sabha to pass a resolution under Article 249 regarding legislation on State List subjects?
opts: Simple majority of members present and voting
Absolute majority of the total membership of the House
Not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting
Two-thirds of total membership plus ratification by half of the states
practiceQuestions.sol: A resolution under Article 249 must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: How long does a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha under Article 249 remain in force initially?
practiceQuestions.sol: A resolution passed under Article 249 remains in force for such period not exceeding one year as may be specified in the resolution. However, it can be extended by another year at a time by passing subsequent resolutions.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is an All-India Service currently operating in India along with the IAS and IPS?
practiceQuestions.sol: There are only three All-India Services in India: Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Forest Service (IFoS). IFoS was created in 1966 under Article 312.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Lok Sabha initiate a proposal to create a new All-India Service under Article 312 independently without the Rajya Sabha?
opts: No, the initiative must originate in the Rajya Sabha
Yes, if recommended by the Prime Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: The power under Article 312 is an exclusive privilege of the Rajya Sabha. Parliament can make law for a new All-India Service only if the Rajya Sabha declares by a resolution to that effect.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional provision deals with the Vice-President of India acting as or discharging the functions of the President, where the Rajya Sabha's presiding officer dynamic comes into play?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 65 provides that the Vice-President shall act as President in case of the occurrence of any vacancy in the office of the President. While acting as President, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of the office of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President of India)?
opts: The President or some person appointed in that behalf by him
The Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 69, every Vice-President shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation.

practiceQuestions.q: Which house has the exclusive power to initiate the removal resolution of the Vice-President of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 67(b), the Vice-President may be removed from his office by a resolution of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council and agreed to by the House of the People (Lok Sabha). However, the resolution can only be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the status of the Rajya Sabha regarding the Money Bill as defined under Article 110?
opts: It can amend or reject a Money Bill.
It has co-equal powers with Lok Sabha on Money Bills.
It has restricted powers; it must return the Money Bill within 14 days with or without recommendations.
It can introduce a Money Bill with prior presidential sanction.
practiceQuestions.sol: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President. The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations and must return it within 14 days.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Articles 249 and 312 considered crucial for maintaining the federal balance in the Indian Constitution, despite appearing to tilt power towards the Centre?
opts: They allow the Union executive to bypass Parliament completely during emergencies.
They give states direct veto power over all central legislations.
They involve the house representing the states (Rajya Sabha) in deciding when national interest overrides state autonomy.
They empower the Supreme Court to strike down arbitrary state laws automatically.
practiceQuestions.sol: Articles 249 and 312 represent unique federal safeguards. Even though they empower Parliament to legislate on State List matters or create All-India Services, the trigger must come from the Rajya Sabha—the chamber specifically representing the federating units (states)—acting by a special majority.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the removal procedure of the Vice-President under Article 67(b) reflect a unique balance between the two houses of Parliament?
opts: Rajya Sabha alone has complete power to remove him without Lok Sabha's consent.
Lok Sabha alone initiates and passes the resolution with Rajya Sabha having no say.
The resolution must originate in the Rajya Sabha with a special majority and be agreed to by the Lok Sabha with a simple majority.
Both houses must pass the resolution concurrently in a joint sitting.
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the privilege and responsibility of initiating their removal rests exclusively with the Rajya Sabha (by an absolute majority of its total members). However, to complete the removal, the Lok Sabha must also agree (by a simple majority), blending the Upper House's institutional control with bicameral parliamentary concurrence.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution under Article 249, and subsequently the Lok Sabha is dissolved?
opts: The Rajya Sabha resolution automatically becomes null and void.
The resolution and any law made by Parliament pursuant to it remain unaffected by the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
The President must promulgate an ordinance to keep the law alive.
The State legislatures can immediately override the central law.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution. A resolution passed under Article 249 gives Parliament the competence to legislate, and laws enacted under it do not lapse upon the dissolution of the Lok Sabha, as continuity is maintained by the Upper House.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Indian Constitution deny the Rajya Sabha the power to vote on Demands for Grants in the Union Budget?
opts: Because Rajya Sabha members are not directly elected by the people.
Because Rajya Sabha does not possess legislative powers over financial matters.
To prevent political deadlocks between the executive and the legislature.
Due to time constraints during the budget session.
practiceQuestions.sol: In a parliamentary democracy, the executive is responsible to the popularly elected lower house (Lok Sabha), which controls the national purse strings. Denying the unelected/indirectly elected Rajya Sabha voting power on Demands for Grants upholds the principle of 'no taxation without representation' and executive accountability to the house representing the direct electorate.

practiceQuestions.q: How does Article 312 safeguard federal administrative integrity while expanding central capabilities?
opts: By allowing the Centre to dismiss state civil servants at will.
By ensuring that a new All-India Service can only be created upon the explicit consent of the states' representatives in Rajya Sabha.
By prohibiting state governments from utilizing AIS officers.
By making AIS officers exclusively accountable to the Supreme Court.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 312 creates a balance: All-India Services unify standards of administration across the country (serving both Union and States), but the Centre cannot unilaterally impose a new All-India Service; it requires the collective consent of the states expressed through a special majority in the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens if a state law enacted prior to a parliamentary law passed under Article 249 is repugnant to the latter?
opts: The state law prevails because of federalism.
The parliamentary law prevails to the extent of repugnancy.
The Supreme Court decides which law applies on a case-by-case basis.
practiceQuestions.sol: When Parliament makes a law on a State List subject pursuant to an Article 249 resolution, such a parliamentary law overrides any inconsistent state law to the extent of the repugnancy, exemplifying the doctrine of parliamentary supremacy in fields authorized by the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of constitutional amendments under Article 368, what is the relative standing of the Rajya Sabha compared to the Lok Sabha?
opts: Rajya Sabha has veto power over constitutional amendments.
Rajya Sabha has co-equal and coordinate power with Lok Sabha; a deadlock must be resolved through defeat of the bill as joint sittings are not permitted.
Rajya Sabha can only delay a constitutional amendment bill for 14 days.
Lok Sabha can override Rajya Sabha's rejection of a constitutional amendment by a simple majority.
practiceQuestions.sol: Constitutional amendment bills under Article 368 must be passed by each House separately by a special majority. There is no provision for a joint sitting under Article 368. Thus, Rajya Sabha holds coordinate and co-equal power with Lok Sabha, making its concurrence mandatory.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution assign the role of Chairman of the Rajya Sabha to the Vice-President rather than electing a member from within the House like the Lok Sabha Speaker?
opts: To ensure that the presiding officer is a neutral, non-partisan figure representing the federal character and outside party politics of the Upper House.
Because the Vice-President has no other constitutional duties.
To give the executive direct administrative control over legislative proceedings.
To reduce government expenditure on parliamentary allowances.
practiceQuestions.sol: By appointing the Vice-President (an official elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament) as the Chairman, the framers ensured that the Rajya Sabha's presiding officer stands above partisan lower-house politics, anchoring the federal and deliberative tone of the Upper House.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Rajya Sabha's exclusive power under Article 249 interact with the principle of cooperative federalism?
opts: It violates cooperative federalism by centralizing all legislative power.
It operationalizes cooperative federalism by allowing states, through their collective representatives in Rajya Sabha, to invite central legislative intervention when national exigencies demand.
It bypasses states entirely to empower the Prime Minister's Office.
It converts India from a federal state into a unitary state permanently.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 249 is not a blunt instrument of central encroachment; rather, it is a mechanism of cooperative federalism where states themselves (via Rajya Sabha) voluntarily cede legislative space to Parliament for a temporary period when national interest so requires.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of the Rajya Sabha having equal power with the Lok Sabha in matters of Impeachment of the President?
opts: It ensures that the President, who is elected by both houses' members (along with state assemblies), can be held accountable by both houses equally.
It allows Rajya Sabha to initiate impeachment without Lok Sabha's consent.
It grants Rajya Sabha members the right to vote in presidential elections.
It makes Rajya Sabha superior to the executive branch.
practiceQuestions.sol: Although nominated members of the Rajya Sabha do not vote in the election of the President, they participate fully in the President's impeachment. This demonstrates that the Upper House shares coordinate judicial/quasi-judicial accountability functions alongside the Lok Sabha over the executive head.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Special Powers of the Rajya Sabha:
1. Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha can authorize Parliament to make laws on any matter enumerated in the State List.
2. Such a resolution must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
3. A resolution passed under Article 249 remains in force indefinitely until expressly repealed by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 249 empowers Rajya Sabha to pass a resolution for State List legislation by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting. Statement 3 is incorrect because a resolution remains in force for a maximum period of one year at a time, though it can be renewed.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding All-India Services under Article 312:
1. The creation of a new All-India Service requires a resolution supported by the Rajya Sabha.
2. The resolution must be passed by a special majority consisting of an absolute majority of total membership and a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
3. The Indian Forest Service (IFoS) was created in 1966 following a resolution under Article 312.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Rajya Sabha must initiate AIS creation). Statement 2 is incorrect because the voting requirement under Article 249 and Article 312 is strictly 'not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting', not an absolute majority of total membership combined with 2/3rd. Statement 3 is correct (IFoS was created in 1966).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Vice-President of India:
1. The resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
2. The resolution in the Rajya Sabha must be passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council.
3. The Lok Sabha's agreement to the Rajya Sabha's resolution is required by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the removal resolution can ONLY be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is correct (passed by a majority of all the then members, i.e., absolute majority of the House). Statement 3 is correct (agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament upon the recommendation of the President.
2. The Rajya Sabha has no power to vote on the Demands for Grants.
3. In case of a deadlock on an ordinary bill, a joint sitting of both houses can be convened by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is correct (Rajya Sabha cannot vote on Demands for Grants). Statement 3 is correct (Article 108 allows joint sittings for ordinary bills).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the exclusive domains of Rajya Sabha:
1. The Rajya Sabha has the power to declare that the creation of a new All-India Service is necessary in the national interest.
2. The Rajya Sabha alone can initiate a proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352.
3. The Rajya Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on State List subjects for a maximum period of two years at a time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Article 312). Statement 2 is incorrect because National Emergency proclamations are issued by the President, and approvals involve both houses or Lok Sabha specially under certain emergency clauses. Statement 3 is incorrect because the maximum period for an Article 249 resolution is 'not exceeding one year' at a time, though extendable.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding financial powers and procedures in Parliament:
1. The Constitution defines a Money Bill under Article 110.
2. If any question arises whether a bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Rajya Sabha Chairman is final.
3. The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days of its receipt, with or without recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Article 110). Statement 2 is incorrect because the decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill or not rests solely with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha Chairman. Statement 3 is correct (14-day rule under Article 109).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Rajya Sabha vis-a-vis Lok Sabha:
1. Rajya Sabha can pass a vote of no-confidence against the Union Council of Ministers.
2. Rajya Sabha has equal power with Lok Sabha in the impeachment of the President of India.
3. Rajya Sabha members participate in the election of the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a no-confidence motion can only be moved in the Lok Sabha, as the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is correct (impeachment power is co-equal). Statement 3 is incorrect because the Speaker is elected only by members of the Lok Sabha from amongst themselves.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional provisions affecting Rajya Sabha:
1. The maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250 by Article 80 of the Constitution.
2. The allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the States and Union Territories is listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
3. Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are chosen from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Article 80 sets max strength at 250). Statement 2 is incorrect because seat allocation to States and UTs in Rajya Sabha is listed in the Fourth Schedule, not the Eighth Schedule (which lists official languages). Statement 3 is correct (Art 80(3) specifies literature, science, art, and social service).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding ordinances and their approval by Parliament:
1. An ordinance promulgated by the President under Article 123 must be approved by both houses of Parliament within six weeks of reassembly.
2. If an ordinance deals with a matter on which Rajya Sabha had previously passed an Article 249 resolution, the legislative domain remains valid.
3. The Rajya Sabha has veto power over ordinance promulgation at the initial stage when the President issues it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Article 123 rules require approval within six weeks of reassembly). Statement 2 is correct because ordinances have the same force as acts of Parliament, and if Parliament is competent via Article 249, the President can issue an ordinance. Statement 3 is incorrect because the President promulgates ordinances on executive advice without any initial legislative veto from Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the federal features and the Rajya Sabha:
1. The primary rationale for conferring special powers under Articles 249 and 312 to the Rajya Sabha is to protect states' rights against unilateral central encroachment while enabling national efficiency.
2. The Rajya Sabha can amend a constitutional amendment bill originating in the Lok Sabha by introducing provisions that affect state federal setups without requiring separate ratification by state legislatures.
3. The Constitution provides that the Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (these articles balance federal protection and administrative needs). Statement 2 is incorrect because any constitutional amendment that affects federal provisions (listed in the proviso to Article 368(2)) requires mandatory ratification by not less than one-half of the state legislatures, regardless of parliamentary house approvals. Statement 3 is correct (Article 83(1) states Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution).
